newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Sexwale may move from politics to business.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Sexwale may move from politics to business.

text.p: Tokyo Sexwale, the premier of South Africa's Gauteng province and one of the most popular leaders of the African National Congress (ANC), is considering quitting politics for a career in business, the ANC said on Thursday.
The statement said no final decision had yet been taken, but that Sexwale had first mooted the idea at a meeting of Gauteng's Provincial Executive Committtee (PEC) in April.

"Sexwale informed us that he had an interest in the business sector, and left it up to the leadership as a collective to take the matter forward...no final decision has been taken," the ANC said in a statement.
The PEC is meeting again in June to discuss the issue.
There has been media speculation that Sexwale, whose Gauteng province is the industrial heartland of South Africa, might join his old friend Mzi Khumalo, now chairman of mining house JCI Ltd.
Another option would be for him to join the Thebe group, where his brother Johnny holds a senior position.

The Business Day newspaper said Sexwale's departure from politics had been rumoured since it became apparent that he had lost the battle for the position of ANC secretary-general, diminishing his chances of moving ahead in politics.
The previous holder of the party post, Cyril Ramaphosa, left politics last year to join black empowerment group New Africa Investments Ltd.
